issues.legal_issue: A female holder who inherits bhumidhari rights does not hold only a life estate merely because the governing law restricts her testamentary disposition or provides special rules of devolution, and may transfer her interest during her lifetime subject to applicable statutory restrictions.
material_facts: The cultivatory lands devolved on a widow after her husband's death, and she later acquired bhumidhari status in those lands under the governing land-reform law.
She gifted the lands to two recipients during her lifetime.
After her death, persons claiming to be reversioners challenged the gift on the ground that she had held only a life estate.

The governing law made a bhumidhar's interest transferable subject to specified restrictions, restricted testamentary disposition for certain female holders, and provided special rules for devolution in certain circumstances.
The law did not designate another person as holding a residuary interest in the lands during the female holder's lifetime.
issues.conclusion: The female bhumidhar held the entire estate and was not limited to a life estate. The restrictions on testamentary disposition and special devolution rules did not prevent her from making an inter vivos gift, subject to the statutory restrictions on transfers; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 152, 169, 171, 172, 172A and 174 of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1951, the transferability of a bhumidhar's interest is subject to specified restrictions, but those restrictions do not themselves qualify the holder's title. A restriction on testamentary disposition or a special rule governing devolution does not imply a life estate or a limitation on inter vivos disposition. Where the Act provides no indication that a residuary interest remains vested in another person, the female holder owns the entire estate. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_gift_as_exceeding_life_estate and female_inherited_bhumidari_rights and female_made_inter_vivos_transfer and governing_law_makes_holder_interest_transferable and governing_law_does_not_designate_residuary_owner and restrictions_address_bequest_or_devolution_not_lifetime_title

predicates.appeal_challenges_gift_as_exceeding_life: The proceeding is an appeal in which claimants assert a reversionary interest and challenge a gift as extending beyond the transferor's lifetime.
predicates.female_inherited_bhumidari_rights: A female holder acquired bhumidhari rights in a holding by inheritance.
predicates.female_made_inter_vivos_transfer: The female holder transferred the holding during her lifetime.
predicates.governing_law_makes_holder_interest_tran: The governing tenure law makes a holder's interest transferable subject to specified restrictions.
predicates.governing_law_does_not_designate_residua: The governing tenure law does not designate another person to hold a residual interest in the holding during the female holder's lifetime.
predicates.restrictions_address_bequest_or_devoluti: The governing law restricts testamentary disposition for certain female holders and provides special rules for devolution without expressly limiting their lifetime title.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a lifetime transfer by a female inheriting bhumidhari rights as exceeding a life estate, and the governing law makes the holder's interest transferable without designating a residuary owner or expressly limiting lifetime title, the female holder may transfer her interest during her life.
